images.title: Diagonals of a calendar square
images.purpose: Show a 2 by 2 square of dates whose two diagonals have equal sums.
images.composition: A single 2 by 2 block of dates in the centre with the two sums below; wide white space.
exact_structure: One 2 by 2 block of four equal square date cells outlined in #2B2B2B, with 12 top left, 13 top right, 19 bottom left, 20 bottom right.
The diagonal 12 and 20 is joined by a thick teal #0072B2 line; the diagonal 13 and 19 is joined by a thick amber #E69F00 line; the two lines cross at the centre.
Below the block two lines: "12 + 20 = 32" in teal #0072B2 and "13 + 19 = 32" in amber #E69F00.
No weekday names, no rest of the calendar, no letter a.
rejection: dates other than 12, 13, 19, 20 in those cells
a sum other than 32 on either diagonal
images.takeaway: Both diagonals of the square add to the same number.
images.description: A 2 by 2 calendar square 12, 13, 19, 20 with its two diagonals joined and both sums equal to 32.
images.context: Shown beside the calendar example text and video.
images.teaching_notes: Add each diagonal yourself before reading the sums.

image_decisions.why: The square isolates the equal diagonal sums, the one idea of this concept.
